2 Disease Testing Using Bayesian Methods

  1. 4.

    [Exam standard] The following data classify 492 patients according to presence or absence of a rare but serious disease as diagnosed by a “gold standard” and by the results of a cheaper but less accurate diagnostic blood test.

    Has disease?
    Yes No Total
    D+ D−
    Test result positive T+ 220 24 244
    Test result negative T− 30 218 248
    Total 250 242 492
    1. (a)

      Define and calculate the Sensitivity and Specificity of the test.

    2. (b)

      Define and calculate the False Positive and False Negative rates. Which one is arguably more of a problem in this example?

    3. (c)

      A patient from the general UK population is selected at random, is tested, and receives a positive test result. In the UK it is known that about 1 in 1000 people have the disease. Calculate the probability that the patient has the disease given the positive test result, P⁢(D+|T+). Comment on your answer.

    4. (d)

      The patient actually had the test done twice and received two positive results, represented by the event T++. Assuming the test results are conditionally independent given disease status, implying that P⁢(T++|D+)=P⁢(T+|D+)2 and P⁢(T++|D−)=P⁢(T+|D−)2, calculate the probability that they have the disease after receiving two positive tests, P⁢(D+|T++).

    5. (e)

      Derive a constraint on the number n of such positive test results that they would have to receive in a row, in order to ensure the probability that they did indeed have the disease is greater than p0.

    6. (f)

      Using the results of part (e) or otherwise, find the lowest possible n for p0=0.4.

    Solution

    1. (a)

      Let T+ and T− be the events that the test is positive and negative respectively, and let D+ and D− be the event that the patient has the disease and does not have the disease respectively.

      Sensitivity is then the probability of testing positive for the disease given the patient has the disease, i.e. P⁢(T+|D+) which from the table is:

      P⁢(T+|D+)=220250

      Specificity is then the probability of testing negative for the disease given the patient does not have the disease, i.e. P⁢(T−|D−) which from the table is:

      P⁢(T−|D−)=218242
    2. (b)

      False Positive is then the probability of testing positive for the disease given the patient does not have the disease, i.e. P⁢(T+|D−) which from the table is:

      P⁢(T+|D−)=24242

      False Negative is then the probability of testing negative for the disease given the patient has the disease, i.e. P⁢(T−|D+) which from the table is:

      P⁢(T−|D+)=30250

      As the disease is serious, a false negative result is arguably more of a problem.

    3. (c)

      We want P⁢(D+|T+) which we get via application of Bayes’ theorem, using prior P⁢(D+)=1/1000:

      P⁢(D+|T+) =P⁢(T+|D+)⁢P⁢(D+)P⁢(T+)

      We can express P⁢(T+) in terms of the partition {D+,D−}, giving

      P⁢(D+|T+) =P⁢(T+|D+)⁢P⁢(D+)P⁢(T+|D+)⁢P⁢(D+)+P⁢(T+|D−)⁢P⁢(D−)
      =(220/250)×(1/1000)(220/250)×(1/1000)+(24/242)×(999/1000)=0.00880

      This is still a very low probability: despite the positive test result, the test is not accurate enough to overcome the small prior probability of having the disease.

    4. (d)

      Assuming P⁢(T++|D+)=P⁢(T+|D+)2 and that P⁢(T++|D−)=P⁢(T+|D−)2 (as given), we have:

      P⁢(D+|T++) =P⁢(T++|D+)⁢P⁢(D+)P⁢(T++|D+)⁢P⁢(D+)+P⁢(T++|D−)⁢P⁢(D−)=
      =P⁢(T+|D+)2⁢P⁢(D+)P⁢(T+|D+)2⁢P⁢(D+)+P⁢(T+|D−)2⁢P⁢(D−)
      =(220/250)2×(1/1000)(220/250)2×(1/1000)+(24/242)2×(999/1000)=0.07306
    5. (e)

      Similarly assuming P⁢(Tn+|D+)=P⁢(T+|D+)n and P⁢(Tn+|D−)=P⁢(T+|D−)n, where Tn+ represents n positive results we have:

      P⁢(D+|Tn+) =P⁢(T+|D+)n⁢P⁢(D+)P⁢(T+|D+)n⁢P⁢(D+)+P⁢(T+|D−)n⁢P⁢(D−)
      =(220/250)n×(1/1000)(220/250)n×(1/1000)+(24/242)n×(999/1000)
      =11+((24×250)/(242×220))n×(999)>p0

      which can be rearranged to give:

      n>log⁡((1−p0)/(999⁢p0))log⁡((24×250)/(242×220))
    6. (f)

      For p0=0.4 we find n>2.978 so the patient would have to receive n=3 positive tests in a row before there was a greater than 0.4 posterior probability that they did indeed have the disease.
